name: Akros
description: Akros is a walled warrior polis of Theros whose patron god is Iroas.

description_citations.text: "The Walls of Akros" by Kelly Digges. Magic Story, Wizards of the Coast, 26 Feb 2014.
"Theros". Magic: The Gathering story profiles, Wizards of the Coast.

summary.text: Akros is a walled warrior polis of Theros whose patron god is Iroas.

citations.text: "The Walls of Akros" by Kelly Digges. Magic Story, Wizards of the Coast, 26 Feb 2014.
"Theros". Magic: The Gathering story profiles, Wizards of the Coast.

bio.text: Iroas is the patron god of the Akroans, and Aesrias is from Akros.

citations.text: "The Walls of Akros" by Kelly Digges. Magic Story, Wizards of the Coast, 26 Feb 2014.
"The Hero of Iroas" by Matt Knicl. Magic Story, Wizards of the Coast, 5 Mar 2014.

bio.text: Minotaurs besieged Akros, and Leandros fell to his knees, too late to prevent the siege from beginning.

citations.text: "The Walls of Akros" by Kelly Digges. Magic Story, Wizards of the Coast, 26 Feb 2014.

bio.text: Later, Lanathos said Elspeth, who might be the latest Champion, was seen at Akros, besieged by minotaurs.

citations.text: "Ajani, Mentor of Heroes" by Kelly Digges. Magic Story, Wizards of the Coast, 17 Dec 2014.

status.text: As of the latest story that mentions it, Akros is besieged by minotaurs.

citations.text: "Ajani, Mentor of Heroes" by Kelly Digges. Magic Story, Wizards of the Coast, 17 Dec 2014.

timeline.summary: Pavios lies awake thinking of Thanasis, knowing his father plans to send him back to Meletis to marry an official's daughter in two days.
timeline.quote: Just two days hence, Pavios's father planned to send him back to Meletis to marry the daughter of a prominent official

citation.text: "Emonberry Red" by Clayton Kroh. Magic Story, Wizards of the Coast, 5 Feb 2014.

timeline.summary: Pavios hides a note for Thanasis telling him to search the coal pile for a gift.
timeline.quote: Pavios rolled up the note and placed it beneath a stone near the door to Thanasis's house.

citation.text: "Emonberry Red" by Clayton Kroh. Magic Story, Wizards of the Coast, 5 Feb 2014.

timeline.summary: Their fathers quarrel and the meetings end, and Pavios's father announces they will return to Meletis for the wedding.
timeline.quote: The following day, the disagreement between their fathers erupted

citation.text: "Emonberry Red" by Clayton Kroh. Magic Story, Wizards of the Coast, 5 Feb 2014.

timeline.summary: Thanasis speaks to Pavios through a crack in the wall at night and asks to meet at midday, thanking him for the gift.
timeline.quote: "I will wait for you," Thanasis said.

citation.text: "Emonberry Red" by Clayton Kroh. Magic Story, Wizards of the Coast, 5 Feb 2014.

timeline.summary: Leandros runs for a day and more past fallen Alamon squads and minotaur bands and reaches Akros at night.
timeline.quote: Occasionally he came upon squads of fallen Alamon

citation.text: "The Walls of Akros" by Kelly Digges. Magic Story, Wizards of the Coast, 26 Feb 2014.

timeline.summary: Leandros discovers the minotaurs have built a wall around Akros to keep the Alamon out while besieging the city.
timeline.quote: A wall. Someone— minotaurs —had built a wall around Akros

citation.text: "The Walls of Akros" by Kelly Digges. Magic Story, Wizards of the Coast, 26 Feb 2014.

timeline.summary: Iroas and Mogis appear as stars above Akros and grapple, absorbed in their own conflict and not helping mortals.
timeline.quote: The twins were interested in each other, not mortals.

citation.text: "The Walls of Akros" by Kelly Digges. Magic Story, Wizards of the Coast, 26 Feb 2014.

timeline.summary: Leandros falls to his knees, too late to prevent the siege of Akros, which begins.
timeline.quote: The siege of Akros had begun.

citation.text: "The Walls of Akros" by Kelly Digges. Magic Story, Wizards of the Coast, 26 Feb 2014.

timeline.summary: In a dream, Pollio ties twine to his family, customers and friends until the ropes grow tight and the crowd's flesh knits into a single mass; he wakes screaming.
timeline.quote: Then, Pollio was part of one amorphous mass of stinking flesh and burning rope

citation.text: "Dreams of the City" by Ken Troop. Magic Story, Wizards of the Coast, 23 Apr 2014.

timeline.summary: Ajani realizes the latest Champion may be Elspeth, and Lanathos says she was seen at Akros, besieged by minotaurs.
timeline.quote: After she slew Polukranos, the Champion was spotted at Akros, which has been besieged by a horde of minotaurs.

citation.text: "Ajani, Mentor of Heroes" by Kelly Digges. Magic Story, Wizards of the Coast, 17 Dec 2014.

timeline.summary: Elektes and six warriors, inspired by Iroas, found Akros after the war between humans and minotaurs.
timeline.quote: Elektes and six other warriors, inspired by the martial doctrine of Iroas , established the polis of Akros, with Elektes as its first king.

citation.text: "Akros", section "Birth of the poleis". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: The king of Olantin besieges Akros for decades after his queen leaves him for the Akroan king.
timeline.quote: What followed was a siege that stretched on for decades.

citation.text: "Akros", section "The Akroan War". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Kytheon Iora leads a gang stealing from the rich and is imprisoned, where Hixus teaches him hieromancy.
timeline.quote: The prison warden, a man named Hixus , taught him Hieromancy, the magic of order.

citation.text: "Akros", section "Kytheon Iora". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Kytheon saves the Kolophon from harpies and cyclopes, defeats the titan of Erebos with Heliod's spear, then throws the spear at Erebos, who kills his irregulars; Kytheon first planeswalks to Bant and becomes Gideon Jura.
timeline.quote: Shocked and shamed by their deaths at his hand, Kytheon then made his first planeswalk to Bant, where he became known as Gideon Jura.

citation.text: "Akros", section "Kytheon Iora". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Xenagos besieges Akros with minotaurs and the Akroans capture him.
timeline.quote: Queen Cymede informed them that the Akroans had captured the satyr Xenagos

citation.text: "Akros", section "The rise and fall of Xenagos". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Cymede offers herself to Keranos, who turns the Deyda River into an elemental that consumes the minotaurs; she ascends to Nyx.
timeline.quote: Cymede was claimed by Keranos as she transformed into a pillar of fire and crimson light and ascended into Nyx

citation.text: "Akros", section "The rise and fall of Xenagos". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Rhordon, aided by Mogis, impales King Anax; Elspeth saves Anax, and Rhordon is washed away by the river.
timeline.quote: The Rageblood quickly defeated Anax by impaling the king through the stomach.

citation.text: "Akros", section "The rise and fall of Xenagos". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Xenagos uses the victory celebration to stage the Great Revel and ascend to godhood.
timeline.quote: Xenagos used the occasion to stage the Great Revel , the final ritual that propelled him to godhood

citation.text: "Akros", section "The rise and fall of Xenagos". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: After the Great Revel Anax dies, Cymede is missing, and their niece Taranika becomes regent.
timeline.quote: the responsibility of leadership fell to their niece, Taranika , who serves as regent

citation.text: "Akros", section "Uncertain succession". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Grieving planeswalkers bury Gideon's breastplate outside Akros as a memorial and Nissa grows an oak.
timeline.quote: Nissa Revane planted an acorn and grew it into a massive oak tree next to the stone

citation.text: "Akros", section "Forsaken". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: During the Phyrexian invasion, the gods and their devotees are compleated and Akros is presumed to have fallen.
timeline.quote: Akros is presumed to have fallen as a metropolis.

citation.text: "Akros", section "Phyrexian invasion". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Mogis sends hordes of minotaurs against Akros, Meletis and Setessa.
timeline.quote: Mogis , the god of slaughter sends hordes of mortal and Nyxborn minotaurs against the human cities Akros , Meletis , and Setessa .

citation.text: "Born of the Gods", section "Flavor and storyline". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Elspeth leads an army of heroes to break the minotaur siege at Akros.
timeline.quote: Elspeth Tirel leads an army of heroes to break the minotaur siege at Akros.

citation.text: "Born of the Gods", section "Flavor and storyline". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: The victory celebration becomes the ritual that launches Xenagos into Nyx as a god; Elspeth is blamed and driven away.
timeline.quote: Elspeth is blamed for his ascension and driven away in disgrace.

citation.text: "Born of the Gods", section "Flavor and storyline". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Elspeth and Daxos travel to Akros, where Xenagos tells her how to destroy the army by raising the river.
timeline.quote: they raised the river that ran through Akros and swept the army away

citation.text: "Daxos", section "Journey into Nyx". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Daxos and Elspeth realize their feelings after the victory celebration.
timeline.quote: Daxos and Elspeth finally realized their feelings for each other

citation.text: "Daxos", section "Journey into Nyx". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Xenagos controls Elspeth, who kills Daxos while lashing out at the Phyrexian Obliterator in her memory.
timeline.quote: only realizing too late that she had just killed Daxos

citation.text: "Daxos", section "Journey into Nyx". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Kytheon, a gang leader in the slums of Akros, steals from the rich to feed the poor.
timeline.quote: taking only what they needed to survive and giving the rest away to the poor

citation.text: "Gideon Jura", section "Adolescence". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Iroas establishes the Iroan Games in Akros to celebrate courage and athletic excellence.
timeline.quote: He established the Iroan Games in Akros to celebrate these ideals

citation.text: "Iroas", section "Description". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Meletis blames Kedarick and declares support for the leonin mission to overthrow him; Akros and Setessa decline aid.
timeline.quote: Meletis formally declared its support for the Leonin mission to overthrow Kedarick

citation.text: "Kedarick VI", section "History". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Keranos circumvents the Silence of the Gods by sending prophetic visions to Queen Cymede, helping her destroy the minotaur army of Rhordon with a steam elemental.
timeline.quote: he circumvented the Silence by sending prophetic visions to Queen Cymede

citation.text: "Keranos", section "History". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: As a reward for her faith, Keranos takes Cymede from Akros shortly before the Great Revel.
timeline.quote: Keranos took her from Akros shortly before the Great Revel

citation.text: "Keranos", section "History". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Leandros's squad is sent to investigate after Eumalos's squad misses its checkpoint, and kills a charging cyclops.
timeline.quote: Leandros's squad was sent there to investigate

citation.text: "Leandros", section "History". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Leandros reaches Akros to find the minotaurs' siege already in progress.
timeline.quote: The minotaurs had built a wall surrounding the city, and he was unable to reach it.

citation.text: "Leandros", section "History". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Pavios moves to Akros, meets Thanasis, and they fall in love.
timeline.quote: Pavios met his neighbor, the blacksmith's son Thanasis, and they fell in love.

citation.text: "Pavios and Thanasis", section "History". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Thanasis gives Pavios his cloak and Pavios gives a short sword; Thanasis speaks of his mother's death and Pavios kisses him.
timeline.quote: Pavios comforted him with a kiss.

citation.text: "Pavios and Thanasis", section "History". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Their fathers forbid the meetings; Pavios sneaks a note and they agree to meet at the cliff.
timeline.quote: Their fathers then forbid them from seeing each other

citation.text: "Pavios and Thanasis", section "History". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Pavios, waiting at the cliff, sees a Fleecemane Lion kill a rabbit; it sees him and he flees into a gorge cave.
timeline.quote: Then the lion raised its head and saw him.

citation.text: "Pavios and Thanasis", section "History". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Pavios returns to find Thanasis dead against the emonberry tree, pierced by the sword he gave him.
timeline.quote: And then he saw Thanasis lying against the emonberry tree, his chest pierced by the sword Pavios had given him.

citation.text: "Pavios and Thanasis", section "History". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Pavios prays to Erebos, who promises they can be together in his realm; Pavios falls on his sword.
timeline.quote: And so, Pavios threw himself on his sword, and for a moment, he laughed.

citation.text: "Pavios and Thanasis", section "History". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Penthikos reports to the king of Akros, who sentences him to be chained to the rocks.
timeline.quote: And so he was chained to the rocks , to die in the sun of Heliod .

citation.text: "Penthikos", section "History". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Penthikos prays for atonement and Erebos answers, freeing him to enter a cave.
timeline.quote: Erebos 's great voice filled the air, acknowledging his prayer

citation.text: "Penthikos", section "History". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Humans and minotaurs wage war over the badlands; Iroas and Mogis and their champions fight, founding Akros and Skophos with Phoberos as border.
timeline.quote: This conflict resulted in the founding of Akros and Skophos

citation.text: "Phoberos", section "History". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Mortals endure and thrive on Theros behind the walls of great poleis, each a bulwark against raging monsters.
timeline.quote: each city-state a bulwark against the raging monsters that roam the more savage places of Theros.

citation.text: "Theros". Magic: The Gathering story profiles, Wizards of the Coast.

timeline.summary: After a Great Revel following the siege of Akros, Xenagos ascended to godhood as god of revels, and Elspeth was scapegoated for Daxos's death and exiled.
timeline.quote: Xenagos held the position of the god of the revels, furthering the chaos and distrust of the established pantheon.

citation.text: "Xenagos", section "Return to Theros". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.
